argument:
Broadcom combines 86% revenue growth with $13.665bn quarterly FCF and a 53.92% GAAP operating margin. Its $35.444bn net debt excluding leases is material, but observed operating-income interest coverage of 20.51x and declining stated debt support manageability. At an estimated 19.38x forward multiple, continued profitable growth could reward ownership without relying only on acquisition-adjusted earnings.

The 46.28x trailing multiple and customer concentration leave sensitivity to an AI spending slowdown. Adjusted earnings exclude recurring SBC, whereas the cash statement provides firmer evidence. The strong quarter should not be annualised into a guaranteed debt-paydown schedule. Reclaimed moving averages and above-average volume support a constructive rebound. The bullish thesis is continued cash-producing demand with financing capacity, not guaranteed delivery of the $34.8bn revenue guidance.
key_points: Measured FCF validates substantial GAAP operating growth.
Interest coverage and declining debt support leverage manageability.
Forward valuation upside depends on concentrated demand continuing.
